title: 1 · The question card, on our chart
what: Piece 1 again, now on the firm's own chart component with the house settings. The candle in question is pointed at (arrow) and painted gold; 'Point at it' switches the pointer off and on.
judge: Is this now our chart? Is the pointer the right way to say 'this candle'? Chart size, question line, choices, button.

title: 2 · The answer card
what: After Check. The same chart now shows the next 20 sessions, a ray at the Kicker's low, right or wrong at the top, the ticker and date, the WHY in your words, three numbers measured from the bars.
judge: Does this teach? Is the why in your voice? Are the three numbers the right three? Toggle right/wrong to see both.

title: 3 · How the chart points at things
what: Six ways to point at a candle on the same chart: arrow, gold paint, white dot, mark the red day too, ray at the close, AVWAP. Each toggles.
judge: Which of these a student actually sees. Which to use for 'look here', which for 'this is the level'. Anything missing (a box around several candles, a zoom)?

title: 4 · Teach first: show, explain, find
what: Three screens before any question: SHOW the Kicker, SAY what makes it one (four rules, in your words), then FIND it: tap the candle on the chart.
judge: Is this how a new idea should be introduced? Too much text, too little? Does tap-the-candle feel like learning or like a gimmick?

title: 5 · Progress and the finish card
what: The strip at the top while answering (green/red/gold, streak at the right), then the finish card: score ring, one sentence about the misses, XP, streak, level, next lesson.
judge: Does finishing feel like anything? Is the ring right, or do you want a chart-shaped progress instead? What should the finish say?

title: 1 · The question card: your chart, an arrow from the left
what: Your own saved chart settings now (hollow candles in your colours, your 9/20/50/200, your volume). The candle is never recoloured: an arrow spaced to its left points at it, with the label further left so nothing is cut off. Switches for the arrow and for marking the red day.
judge: Is THIS our chart now? Is the arrow spaced right, and is the label readable? Anything else on the card?

title: 2 · The whole loop, played like a game
what: Three real questions on three real charts (Kicker, Slingshot, Launchpad). Pick, Check: a sheet slides up green or red with a pop, +10 XP flies, the bar fills, a combo counts, the next 20 sessions appear with the line that mattered. Wrong answers shake and show the right one. Ends on a result card. Play it through.
judge: Does it FEEL like Duolingo yet? What is missing from the feel: sound, a mascot, hearts, a timer, bigger reactions? What is too much?

title: 3 · The answer card with the trade in it
what: Why in your words, then IF YOU TRADED IT: entry over the Kicker high, stop under its low, the distance, the size the house rule gives at 0.5% risk, the shares on a $25k account, whether it filled and whether the stop held, best move and close in 20 sessions. Entry and stop lines drawn on the chart.
judge: Are these the right entry and stop tactics for a Kicker? Right numbers to show? Too much for a reveal, or exactly what a student needs?

title: 4 · Teach by replay, then find it
what: The chart plays forward one day at a time and stops itself on the red day (why it matters) and on the Kicker (what to see), with a slider to scrub. Then the chart runs on 20 more sessions and the member has to tap the Kicker.
judge: Is replay the right way to teach a setup? Speed? Do the two stops say enough? Is find-it a real test now that the candle is not the last one?

title: 5 · The frame and the finish
what: The frame while answering: a glowing bar, a combo counter, +XP pops. Then the finish: the ring and XP count up, confetti on a strong score, chips for what you learned, your misses with the one-line fix, next lesson.
judge: Does finishing feel like something now? What would make you open it again tomorrow?

title: 1 · The question on the FULL UCT chart widget

Two candles of gap at the right. Switch Full / Compact / Mini; mini can hide the ticker; 1, 2 or 3 candle gap.

what: Five questions in three forms. NAME it: four choices, the right one in a different slot each time, None of these always offered, no arrow, the chart just ends on the day. FIND it: the chart already ran on, tap the candle that triggered the trade. ENTER it: your tactics in your words (ORB, or the break of the previous day's high) against three wrong ones. The game feel stays.

The stop under the low and the sizing stay marked as proposed.

It stops itself on the red day and on the Kicker, then runs 20 sessions so you watch the line hold. Then you find it.
judge: Is the playback good now? Speed defaults? Should it stop by itself or run through? Anything the chart's own Time Machine does better?
